text:
elaine: quick thread for Orion Health POC. They want: streaming SDK (go + python), function/tool calling to hit their EHR search endpoint, and deterministic structured JSON for downstream ingestion. Also asked about SSO/SAML, customer KMS (on-prem), and a monthly estimate for ~400 sustained QPS. Any obvious no-gos? :wave:

 theo: sounds fine. Main constraints: 1) sustained 400 QPS with streaming + tool calls -> recommend Dedicated. 2) tool-call latency variability (EHR search) could blow up tail latency; need async tool call pattern + timeouts. 3) SAML/on-prem KMS are policy/legal ops work, not infra blockers.

 rachel: for structured outputs we usually push a JSON schema and enforce model responses via function-calling + schema validation. Can provide a sample schema they can plug into their pipeline. Also note: we can return results in chunked streaming but final object must validate against schema client-side.

 rachel: sample minimal schema to start with:
```
{ "type":"object", "properties": { "patient_id": {"type":"string"}, "action": {"type":"string"}, "records": {"type":"array"} }, "required":["patient_id","action"] }
```

 ivan: SDK and adapter notes: Go sdk supports streaming frames and tool-call hooks. I'll prepare a tiny adapter that translates a tool_call into a promise-like callback so the model can continue streaming partials while we resolve the external call. We'll include retry/backoff and a max-wait of 2s before returning a fallback.

 elaine: can we see the adapter snippet? also need a short curl/ws example for their infra folks.

 ivan: go snippet (stream+tool stub):
```
client := redwood.NewStreamClient(os.Getenv("RW_TOKEN"))
client.OnToolCall(func(call ToolCall) ToolResult {
  // call EHR search with timeout
  res, err := ehr.Search(call.Payload)
  if err != nil { return ToolResult{Action:"noop", Payload: map[string]interface{}{}\\
```
